text: {"frames":["\"Follow the blue light,\" said the boatman, and then he was gone. A lantern on a barge burned blue over the lower canal of the Tower, and it drifted on before anyone could reach it. Someone had drawn the way on a sheet of plan paper: {a} cells along the lock wall, {b} cells past the windmill, and {c} cells up the rope ladder. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the route the blue light took?","Something was missing from the attic shelf: the brass bell of the old spinning wheel. Behind the cupboard, someone was humming an old song, very quietly, as if to keep himself company. Pim found chalk marks on the floor that led away from the cupboard, and they made a route on a plan. The route ran {a} cells along the beam, {b} cells across the loft, and {c} cells down the stairwell. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the route that leads to the bell?","Lot ran down the stairs into the mill cellar, and a cold draught blew up past her ankles. Faraway music came from somewhere under the floorboards, thin and sweet. She found a rolled plan of the old tunnels tucked under a sack of flour. The tunnel went {a} cells along the sluice, {b} cells under the dyke, and {c} cells to the room where the music was. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the tunnel from the sluice to the music?","A low gurgle came from the lock, like something breathing in its sleep. The water rose a little, then sank, then rose again, and it smelled of wet rope and tar. Femke pulled a soggy chart out of the lock keeper's box. The path around the lock was marked in three parts: {a} cells along the quay, {b} cells over the footbridge, and {c} cells round the sluice gate. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the path around the lock?","Every window of the crooked house with the hoist beam was glowing, yet nobody was inside. Bas stood in the street and counted the lit panes twice, and then the lamps flickered. A note hung on the hoist hook, written in pencil: Walk my way and you will find the bell. The walk on the plan ran {a} cells along the canal, {b} cells past the tulip field, and {c} cells to the back door. Each cell of the plan is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the walk the note describes?"]}
